newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares bounce off lows on fund buying.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares bounce off lows on fund buying.

text.p: Late buying by domestic financial institutions offset early losses and pushed share prices to a modestly higher close on the Delhi Stock Exchange, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 1.03 points higher at 757.41. At mid-session the index had been down 3.23 points at 753.35.
"Purchases by domestic financial institutions reversed early trends and wiped out most of the losses," said Arun Aggarwal of brokers Jai Mata Securities.
Reliance Industries, after dropping to a mid-session low of 199 rupees, ended 1.65 rupees higher at 203.65 on speculative buying, brokers said.
State Bank of India rose 3.70 rupees to 272.65, while Oriental Bank of Commerce edged up 0.35 rupee to 82 following late buying by the financial houses, they said.
Larsen and Toubro inched up 0.25 rupee to 245.25, and ACC closed seven rupees higher at 2,025.
ITC quoted 2.15 rupees higher at 290.10, while Hindustan Lever surged eight rupees to 816 on fund buying, brokers said.
However, TELCO bucked the trend to close nine rupees lower at 616 on profit selling, they said.
